newsitem.title: FRANCE: Vallourec to set Mannesman venture.
newsitem.headline: Vallourec to set Mannesman venture.

text.p: French steels group Vallourec said on Monday it planned to group its unwelded stainless tubes business with that of German firm Mannesmannrohren-Werke.
Vallourec said in a statement Mannesmannrohren-Werke would buy from Usinor Sacilor a 21 percent stake in Vallourec, becoming its main shareholder.
Usinor currently owns 27.7 percent of Vallourec.

In a separate statement Usinor Sacilor said the sale of 21 percent of the capital of Vallourec and of Vallourec convertible bonds would be made through the exercise of buy options at conditions "very close to the market value of the stock in early February."
Upon completion of the transaction, Usinor will retain a little over five percent of the capital of Vallourec.
The transaction must be approved by the supervisory boards of Vallourec and Mannesmannrohren Werke and by national and European regulatory authorities, Usinor said.
The new unit will combine the unwelded steel tubes business of Mannesmannrohr, Mannesmannrohren-Werke Sachsen, Vallourec Industries, Petrole et Gaz of Valtubes, and the laminating plant of Valti.
The venture will later acquire the stainless tubes business of Mannesmann SA in Brazil.
It will also control 30 percent of the steel plant of Huttenwerke Krupp Mannesmann GmbH.
The new company will have a turnover of some nine billion francs, excluding the Brazilian business, lifting Vallourec's consolidated turnover to some 13 billion francs.
Vallourec will have control of 55 percent of the venture and Mannesmannrohren-Werke the balance.
Vallourec and Mannesmann will be equally represented on the board of directors but a Vallourec official will head the board.
